paper.title: Mixture of Orthogonal Decomposition for Semantically Generalisable Multimodal Deepfake Detection with Deepfake Manifold Disentanglement
paper.abstract: Multimodal deepfakes have caused significant social issues and raised substantial security concerns. Generalisably detecting these multimodal deepfakes can be factored into two intricately intertwined subspaces, i.e., the semantic subspace and the forgery subspace. However, contemporary deepfake detection methods predominantly focus on pursuing generalisability within the forgery subspace, usually neglecting the influences of the semantic subspace. Additionally, existing deepfake detection algorithms categorise all deepfakes generated by various deepfake generation techniques under a single ''Fake'' category. This methodology may fail to account for the unique characteristics and extensive aspects of various deepfake generation techniques. To address all these challenges, we propose an innovative sparsely-gated Mixture of ORthogonal Decomposition (MoORD) deepfake detection model. Whilst the orthogonal decomposition parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique guarantees the generalisation performance of deepfake detection, the MoORD structure further enhances our model's semantic generalisability. Our MoORD model further learns product manifold representations to disentangle the ''Fake'' category into separate sub-categories of various deepfake generation techniques.
